---
title: "El Niño / PDO"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
```

Two Pacific climate indices:

- `nino34_anom`: monthly Niño 3.4 SST anomaly, unsmoothed, NOAA CPC (1950–present). Source: <https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/> (`ersst5.nino.mth.91-20.ascii`)
- `pdo`: monthly Pacific Decadal Oscillation index, NOAA NCEI (1854–present, joined to the overlapping range). Source: <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/pdo/>

Both are monthly and unsmoothed — unlike ONI's 3-month rolling mean, which would introduce autocorrelation by construction and violate `model-assumptions.qmd`. The ENSO–PDO correlation is known to be non-stationary across decadal climate regimes (e.g. the 1976–77 Pacific climate shift), making this a natural real-data test case for ECE.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: elnino-load

nino <- read_table(
  "../data/real-data/elnino/nino34-raw.txt",
  skip = 1,
  col_names = c("year", "month", "nino12", "nino12_anom", "nino3", "nino3_anom",
                "nino4", "nino4_anom", "nino34", "nino34_anom")
) |>
  select(year, month, nino34_anom)

pdo <- read_table(
  "../data/real-data/elnino/pdo-raw.txt",
  skip = 2,
  col_names = c("year", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
                "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")
) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "month_name", values_to = "pdo") |>
  mutate(month = match(month_name, month.abb)) |>
  select(year, month, pdo)

X <- inner_join(nino, pdo, by = c("year", "month")) |>
  arrange(year, month) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month))) |>
  filter(pdo > -99)
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-elnino-raw
#| fig-cap: "Niño 3.4 anomaly and PDO index, monthly."

X |>
  select(date, nino34_anom, pdo) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Niño 3.4 Anomaly vs. PDO Index", x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: elnino-matrix

X_mat <- as.matrix(X[, c("nino34_anom", "pdo")])

win <- 25 # matches the window used in mental-load.qmd
roll_mat <- apply(X_mat, 2, function(col) rolling_mean(col, win))
colnames(roll_mat) <- colnames(X_mat)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-elnino}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_mat[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  lines(roll_mat[, i], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Month index (1950–present)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R acf-elnino-naive}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  resid_i <- na.omit(X_mat[, i] - roll_mat[, i])
  acf(resid_i, main = "", xlab = "", ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i])
}
mtext("Lag (months)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R acf-elnino-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_sip_acf(X_mat)
```

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R trend-elnino-naive}
#| echo: false

```

```{R trend-elnino-invariant}
#| echo: false

```

## Variance

```{R variance-elnino}
#| echo: false

plot_ece_variance(X_mat, window = win)
```

:::

Naive ACF (base-R `acf()`) now runs on rolling-mean residuals (`X - roll_mat`, same `win = 25` fit shown on the Plot tab), not raw levels — the raw-level version was misleading, since a flat global mean is an underfit for a series with real multi-year structure, and that underfit shows up as inflated apparent autocorrelation rather than genuine short-lag dependence. Even after removing the rolling mean, lag-1 autocorrelation is still ~0.90 (`nino34_anom`) and ~0.66 (`pdo`) — some real short-lag persistence remains — but it now decays to zero within about 5–6 lags (versus staying elevated well past lag 20 on raw levels), then mildly overshoots negative for a few lags, a typical ringing artifact of removing a smooth filter. Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF (`SIP::SIP.acf`): both series read as uncorrelated at every lag. `SIP.acf` discounts mean-shift-induced autocorrelation, so the gap suggests the naive values (raw or residual) are still partly inflated by mean structure the rolling mean didn't fully capture, not pure error autocorrelation — though this doesn't prove the residual process is white.

Faded bars in the Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF mark lags where `SIP.acf`'s own difference-based variance estimate came out negative and fell back to the naive `var(x)` (see `plot_sip_acf()`/`sip_acf_with_fallback()` in `R/plot-helpers.R`). Since `var(x)` is inflated by mean shifts relative to the variance `SIP.acf` is meant to use, those lags' values rest on a mismatched denominator and are less trustworthy than the rest. For `nino34_anom` every lag shown falls back (fully faded); for `pdo` none do.

Naive Trend (`plot_naive_terms`) removes a rolling mean per series, then plots the raw product of those residuals (gray) with its own rolling mean on top (blue) against the global mean (dashed) — same grammar as the Mean-Shift-Invariant Trend (`plot_ece_terms`), but mean-removal is a rolling mean instead of ECE's difference-based construction. `plot_ece_terms` is what ECE's test statistic actually uses, and it still drifts from its global mean over multi-year stretches — some non-stationarity survives mean-shift removal either way.

## Downsampling

Keep every 3rd observation (`k = 3`), matching `mental-load.qmd` and ENSO/PDO's typical 3-month tracking cadence.

```{R downsample-elnino}
#| echo: false

k_ds <- 3
idx  <- seq(1, nrow(X_mat), by = k_ds)
X_ds <- X_mat[idx, ]

win_ds <- 25 # same fixed window as the full-sample case
roll_mat_ds <- apply(X_ds, 2, function(col) rolling_mean(col, win_ds))
colnames(roll_mat_ds) <- colnames(X_ds)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-elnino-downsampled}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_ds[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_ds)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  lines(roll_mat_ds[, i], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Index (every 3rd month)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R acf-elnino-downsampled-naive}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  resid_i <- na.omit(X_ds[, i] - roll_mat_ds[, i])
  acf(resid_i, main = "", xlab = "", ylab = colnames(X_ds)[i])
}
mtext("Lag (every 3rd month)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R acf-elnino-downsampled-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_sip_acf(X_ds)
```

:::

## Trend

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R trend-elnino-downsampled-naive}
#| echo: false

plot_naive_terms(X_ds, window = win_ds)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R trend-elnino-downsampled-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_ece_terms(X_ds, window = win_ds)
```

:::

## Variance

```{R variance-elnino-downsampled}
#| echo: false

plot_ece_variance(X_ds, window = win_ds)
```

:::

Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF stays near-zero before and after downsampling. Naive ACF (on rolling-mean residuals) drops further with downsampling: lag-1 autocorrelation ~0.90→0.75 (`nino34_anom`), ~0.66→0.51 (`pdo`). `k = 3` is not enough to whiten either series — ENSO/PDO persistence runs months to years, unlike the sensor-artifact case in `mental-load.qmd`. A larger stride or explicit pre-whitening would be needed to satisfy the naive no-autocorrelation assumption; the mean-shift-invariant view suggests less of that persistence reaches the quantity ECE actually uses.

The Variance tab (`plot_ece_variance`) plots each column's own diagonal ECE term (`lag_term(x, x)`) the same way the Trend tab plots the off-diagonal — this is the quantity whose average is the "variance" that showed up negative/near-zero in `ece.cov()`'s diagonal at small `L`. For `nino34_anom` (downsampled), the rolling mean hovers at or below zero for most of the series, not just near the edges — a persistent property of the whole record, not a one-off event. There is a large late spike near the very end of the series, but with only ~1–2 points out of ~306 involved, it has little effect on the global mean; trimming that stretch earlier left the `L`-instability essentially unchanged. `pdo`'s diagonal term, by contrast, stays mostly at or above zero throughout. This is the more complete picture behind why `ece.cov(X_ds, L=2)`'s diagonal for `nino34_anom` comes out negative: not an outlier, but a chronic near-zero equivariant variance driven by the series' own strong short-lag autocorrelation.
